biography.plain_text: Robert E. Spatt is an American corporate lawyer and retired partner of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett in New York. Educated at Brown and Michigan Law School, he advised companies and boards on mergers, acquisitions and governance during three decades of practice. He subsequently joined the board of the humanitarian organisation Action Against Hunger.

long_biography.plain_text:
Corporate lawyer Robert Spatt started work at Simpson Thacher while still studying for the bar examination. He needed to pay the rent on his first New York apartment. By his fifth or sixth year as an associate, he was negotiating merger agreements largely independently. His approach centred on understanding what each party needed and finding terms both could accept.

Spatt also helped other practitioners examine how deals are structured, serving as co-chairman of the Tulane Corporate Law Institute. He repeatedly revised The Four Ring Circus, an analysis of competing takeover bids. The work examined what happens when another bidder intervenes after companies have already agreed a merger.
